analysis:
Integration of 16 units. The PR moves the macOS jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml (test-provider shards 1-3, summary, SDK, cluster checks, cluster shards, GPU shards, focused) from the literal blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27 runner to runs-on: fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[lane]. The route job now requests per-lane macos_arm64 grants gated on classifier outputs (patch hunk at ci.yml lines 50-64). The remaining changes are docs (build.md, test.md, changelog fragment) and offline CI test scripts (test-darkbloom-route.py, test-ci-component-paths.py, test-cluster-test-plan.py, test-provider-ci-workflow.py). No provider runtime, wire protocol, key, attestation, App Attest, or prefix-cache code changed, so T-041, TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012 and TB-013 are not affected.

Controls preserved per the replayed patch and unit analyses: the workflow keeps contents: read and the route job has permissions {}; checkouts use persist-credentials: false; cache saves are limited to master/dev pushes (SAVE_CACHES); the tests still assert no secrets, no id-token, an explicit timeout, and fallback labels for routed jobs; release and credentialed workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners (build.md line 300, UNROUTED tests); fork PRs keep the fallback; exact-label grants are required; and the gate truth table is unchanged.

Unverified contracts, not findings: darkbloom-route.yml, the plane's approval and branch admission, and the Darkbloom macOS sandbox isolation were not supplied. Push runs on master/dev on a routed runner can save GitHub Actions caches, so a less trusted sandbox could poison caches that later runs restore. Whether cache keys are isolated per runner class and whether the plane admits only trusted branches cannot be confirmed here. This is a CI supply-chain question outside the provider threat model, so a human check of the route workflow and plane admission is advisable. The replayed integration source covers only part of the PR (49 units omitted), which is a coverage limit.
